documents.text: Material LCWT401: R=1.25cm, H=4.0cm. T_solidus=62.0C, T_liquidus=72.0C, mushy zone mid=67.0C. k=0.25W/mK, rho=990.0kg/m3. Main defect: Surface sink mark (ヒケ) at top fill point due to shrinkage during solidification
Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap: Heat-retention cap applied near top surface only. Air cooling at room temperature. Result: Slight ヒケ observed — better than no cap but not perfect

Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap reheat schedule: [{"t_min": 10, "duration_min": 1, "method": "Hot air"}, {"t_min": 14, "duration_min": 1, "method": "Hot air"}, {"t_min": 19, "duration_min": 1, "method": "Hot air"}]
Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap at 0min: Bulk fluid, liquid state
Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap at 10min: Bulk fluid, liquid state
Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap at 20min: Slight fluidity, partial gel
Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap at 30min: No fluidity; slight central sinking
Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap at 40min: Top solidified; slight central sinking (bulk still warm)
Trial 1 — Heat Retention Cap at next_day: Depression on top surface from volume shrinkage (ヒケ observed)

Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat: Room-temperature cooling. 3 × hot-air reheat pulses (1 min each, 90°C) on top surface only. Result: ヒケ still present despite 3× reheat. Surface healed but re-solidified with indent.
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat key insight: Short (1 min) pulses at 90°C partially re-melt surface but indent re-forms during final solidification. Longer dwell or higher temperature needed.

Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat reheat schedule: [{"t_min": 10, "t_end_min": 11, "T_C": 90, "method": "Hot air 1 min"}, {"t_min": 14.5, "t_end_min": 15.5, "T_C": 90, "method": "Hot air 1 min"}, {"t_min": 19, "t_end_min": 20, "T_C": 90, "method": "Hot air 1 min"}]
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at 10min: Partial solidification; initial central indentation forming
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at 11min: Surface re-melted (after reheat 1)
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at 14.5min: Partial solidification; central indentation again
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at 15.5min: Surface re-melted (after reheat 2)
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at 19min: Partial solidification; central indentation
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at 20min: Surface re-melted (after reheat 3)
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at 25min: Loss of fluidity
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at 30min: Fully solidified
Trial 2 — RT Cool + Top-Surface Reheat at next_day: No internal voids. Depression on top surface (volume shrinkage). ヒケ still present.
Production Line (Back-fill): Actual CBIC production with back-filling and cold air + 5× hot-air pulses (20 sec each). Result: Acceptable product within 24.5 min. Minor ヒケ at top surface.

Production Line (Back-fill) key insight: 5 × 20 sec pulses at 100°C during mushy zone traversal (not after). Cold air (16°C) starts at t≈21.3 min for final solidification. Total 24.5 min — well within 30-min target.
Production Line (Back-fill) reheat schedule: {"count": 5, "duration_sec": 20, "T_C": 100, "approximate_start_times_min": [0.57, 1.47, 5.17, 7.23, 9.73]}

Rule: Reheat must reach mushy zone (62–72°C) to be effective. Evidence: Trial 2: surface re-melts at 90°C → heals but re-forms ヒケ. Trial 1: slow cap cool avoids rapid quench.. Action: Use T_reheat ≥ 75°C for entry into mushy, ≥ 80°C for reliable healing.

Rule: Total process time must be ≤ 30 min. Evidence: Client target. Production line achieves 24.5 min.. Action: Multi-zone step cooling reduces total time vs single RT cool (which takes 30+ min alone).

Rule: Biot number ≤ 0.5 ensures uniform radial cooling. Evidence: High Bi (> 0.5) causes large T_surface - T_core gradient → higher ヒケ risk.. Action: Keep h_cool ≤ 8 W/m²K for R=1.25 cm (Bi = h×R/k = 8×0.0125/0.25 = 0.4).

Rule: Mushy zone traversal speed is critical. Evidence: Production line spends ~10 min in mushy zone (62–72°C). Rapid quench increases DI.. Action: Design zones to slow the transition through 62–72°C. Target T_core ≈ T_surface in mushy.

Rule: Short reheat pulses (< 1 min) are ineffective for healing. Evidence: Production uses 20 sec × 5 pulses. Trial 2 uses 1 min × 3 pulses — still ヒケ.. Action: Either: (a) many short pulses during mushy traverse, OR (b) longer sustained reheat (≥ 10 min at ≥ 80°C).

Rule: Cold air (16°C) should start only after bulk reaches below solidus (< 62°C). Evidence: Production: cold air at t=21.3 min when T_bulk ≈ 55°C (below solidus).. Action: Premature cold air application increases DI significantly.

DRL optimal targets: production-ready peak DI <= 0.1; cracks begin at 0.25 (CAUTION), WARNING from 0.5, CRITICAL from 0.8. Total time target <= 30 min. Recommended 3 zones. T_reheat range [75, 110]C, recommended 80C. h_cool range [3, 10] W/m2K.
Production-optimal schedule: {"T_fill_C": 74.9, "zones": 3, "T_zone1_C": 65, "T_zone2_C": 50, "T_zone3_C": 37, "T_reheat_C": 80, "t_reheat_min": 10, "total_min": 30, "DI_expected": 0.1}

Damage Index (DI) scale: SAFE 0.0-0.25 (top surface within limits; no sink marks below 0.15, faint marks possible from 0.15); CAUTION 0.25-0.5 (sink marks and the first cracks); WARNING 0.5-0.8 (clear sink marks and cracks); CRITICAL 0.8-1.0 (severe defects, production reject)
